impact_scope.description: The anchored existing public callable ares_queue_wait_empty changes its timeout-deadline calculation from inline arithmetic to a one-hop internal helper that normalizes microseconds. Its signature, caller-supplied timeout value, configuration, lifecycle, and call order are unchanged.

evidence: In S0, ares_queue_wait_empty already exists as a public callable taking channel and timeout_ms.
H0 exercises DNS parsing, DNS writing, query creation, and server-CSV parsing, but never calls ares_queue_wait_empty or constructs its queue-wait lifecycle.
In S1, the identical ares_queue_wait_empty callable and caller-facing parameters remain in place.
H0 remains unchanged and still does not call ares_queue_wait_empty; the new ares_timeval_add argument is supplied automatically inside that existing callable.

new_harness_obligation.description: S1 adds no caller-visible harness action beyond the already-omitted ares_queue_wait_empty call path; the helper delegation and timeval normalization are internal implementation behavior.
evidence: The caller still supplies only the same channel and timeout_ms arguments.
No new entry point, caller-controlled buffer or value, call-order transition, or runtime/compile-time configuration is required.
H0 would need the same direct API exposure in both S0 and S1.

reason: The principal comparison unit is the mechanically anchored ares_queue_wait_empty timeout path, not the newly extracted internal helper as an independent harness target. H0 omits that same callable before and after, and S1 does not change how a harness reaches or controls it. Therefore the exposure gap is true on both sides and is UNCHANGED.
